mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.25%) indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days without regime dependence.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 0.25%, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows falls below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 9.0% signals weak labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 9.0%, or Rank IC over 3-year windows remains below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous expansion in housing starts (HOUST > 550k) and retail sales (RSAFS > 390k) indicates robust consumer demand that accelerates corporate revenue growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days through earnings momentum.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST > 550k and RSAFS > 390k, or interaction term Rank IC falls below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 2.5% YoY), rising federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS > 0.25%) signal aggressive monetary tightening that compresses equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 2.5% YoY and FEDFUNDS > 0.25%, or interaction term Rank IC remains below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained upward trend in housing starts (HOUST > 560k) reflects improving residential construction activity that boosts consumer confidence and immediate market sentiment, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST > 560k, or Rank IC over 3-year windows falls below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production falling below 90.0 indicates manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate output and supply chain efficiency, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days through earnings deterioration.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO < 90.0, or Rank IC over 3-year windows remains below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strong employment growth (PAYEMS > 100k monthly) and low unemployment (UNRATE < 5.0%) signals a tight labor market that increases consumer spending power and corporate profit margins, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS > 100k and UNRATE < 5.0%, or interaction term Rank IC falls below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In recessionary regimes (GDPC1 growth < 0.5% annualized), declining industrial production (INDPRO < 95.0) confirms economic contraction that triggers earnings revisions downward, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 growth < 0.5% and INDPRO < 95.0, or interaction term Rank IC remains below 0.03.
